fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output: A code carries four data bits and is to detect up to three bit errors and correct one. Give extra parity bits and minimum distance.
fingerprint.procedure: Ordinary Hamming(7, 4) uses three parity bits and has distance three, enough for single-error correction but only two-error detection as a code-distance property. Adding one overall parity bit produces extended Hamming(8, 4), with four redundancy bits and distance four. Distance d detects up to d−1 errors and corrects floor((d−1)/2), giving three and one here. These are separate guarantees: a decoder that automatically corrects a one-bit-looking syndrome can miscorrect some triple errors. Guaranteed simultaneous classification of every one-bit versus three-bit error requires a stronger distance condition than this standard detect-or-correct interpretation.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output: Fill in why a handshake protocol provides reliable transfer for each data item sent.
fingerprint.procedure: A request or data-valid signal tells the receiver that a transfer is available. The receiver responds with an acknowledgment after accepting the item, allowing the sender to withdraw it or send the next one. This coordinates devices with different or variable speeds without assuming a fixed delay is always sufficient. The basic handshake prevents loss from timing mismatch; it does not alone detect arbitrary corruption of data bits. Error-detecting codes or retransmission rules would be separate protocol features.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output: Are start/stop bits used for error detection, correction, synchronization, or slowing communication?
fingerprint.procedure: In asynchronous serial communication, the start transition establishes the beginning of a character frame and lets the receiver align its sampling clock. Stop bits return the line to an idle state and separate frames. They are framing overhead rather than payload. A receiver may report a framing error when an expected stop bit is absent, but these bits are not a general error-correcting code. Slowing the payload rate is a consequence of overhead, not their purpose.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output: Find minimum Hamming distance of {000000,010101,101010,000111,011001,111111}; GateForum omits 101010.
fingerprint.procedure: Hamming distance counts differing bit positions. For example 010101 and 000111 differ in exactly two positions, so the minimum is at most two. Checking the other distinct pairs finds no pair differing in one position; their distances are two, three, four or six. Hence the minimum is two. The additional GFG codeword 101010 has distances three or six to some words and does not introduce a distance-one pair. Removing it, as the alternate does, therefore leaves the same minimum, though the reproduced code sets are not identical.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output:
A network uses the printed subnet mask 255.255.31.0. Which pair of addresses could belong to that network?
A. 172.57.88.62 and 172.56.87.233
B. 10.35.28.2 and 10.35.29.4
C. 191.203.31.87 and 191.234.31.88 [GFG; GateForum prints 191.03.31.87 as the first address.]
D. 128.8.129.43 and 128.8.161.55
The printed mask is noncontiguous; apply its literal bitwise AND, not an assumed CIDR repair.
fingerprint.procedure:
1. Membership under the printed mask requires address 1 AND mask = address 2 AND mask. Its first two 255 octets preserve both first octets, while the final zero octet discards the host's last octet.
2. A fails because 57≠56 in octet two; C fails because 203≠234. B's first two octets match, but 28 AND 31=28 and 29 AND 31=29, so it fails too.
3. For D, 129=10000001₂ and 161=10100001₂. AND with 31=00011111₂ gives 00000001₂ for both. Both network values are 128.8.1.0.
4. Thus the literal calculation selects D. Because 00011111 is not a contiguous prefix-mask octet, this is not a valid ordinary CIDR mask; that caveat must remain explicit.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output:
A broadcast LAN is 2 km long, has bandwidth 10^7 bits/s and uses CSMA/CD. Signals propagate along its wire at 2×10^8 m/s. What is the minimum packet size usable on the network?

fingerprint.procedure:
1. In the worst case a remote transmitter starts just before hearing the first transmitter. The collision indication must travel back, requiring nearly a full round-trip propagation time.
2. One-way propagation is 2000/(2×10^8)=10^−5 s=10 μs. Therefore a frame must last at least 20 μs for collision detection while transmission is still in progress.
3. At 10^7 bits/s the minimum length is 10^7×20×10^−6=200 bits. Divide by eight to convert to bytes: 25 bytes.
4. None of the listed numerical byte sizes equals that theoretical minimum, so D. The 200 in the computation is bits, not the 200-byte option C.

fingerprint.setup_constraints_requested_output:
A sends data to B over a full-duplex link using a sliding-window protocol. Send and receive windows each hold five packets. Data packets are 1000 bytes and take 50 μs to transmit. ACKs travel only B→A and have negligible transmission time. One-way propagation is 200 μs. What is maximum achievable throughput?
A. 7.69×10^6 bps
B. 11.11×10^6 bps
C. 12.33×10^6 bps
D. 15.00×10^6 bps
Both reproductions print packet size in bytes and options in bits per second.
fingerprint.procedure:
1. The raw link rate is 1000×8/(50×10^−6)=160×10^6 bits/s.
2. Packet 1 finishes leaving A at 50 μs and reaches B at 250 μs. Its immediate ACK returns to A at 450 μs. Meanwhile A can send packets 1–5 during 0–250 μs and must wait before sending packet 6 at 450 μs.
3. The ACKs then space subsequent transmissions 50 μs apart, giving recurrent batches of five packets per 450 μs. Window-limited throughput=5×1000×8/(450×10^−6)=88.888... Mbit/s, below the raw rate.
4. No option matches. 5000/(450 μs)=11.111... million bytes/s, numerically close to B but with the wrong unit. Accepting B would silently discard the factor eight, so the baseline unanswered status is retained.
